description: Corpus-driven proposal hypotheses. All new capability definitions require governed research and human review before publication.

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: The existing capabilities describe particular uses of Python. A Python requirement does not establish API, data-processing, AI, or RAG work.

new_capability.label: Python development
new_capability.definition: Implementation, maintenance, or substantial scripting in the Python programming language.
does_not_prove: A generic programming claim without Python evidence
Use of a Python-based product without writing Python
boundaries: Does not imply backend, data engineering, AI, or automation without context

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: SQL querying is distinct from schema design, generic data processing, and database authorization.

new_capability.label: SQL querying
new_capability.definition: Writing, reviewing, and optimizing SQL queries against relational data stores.
does_not_prove: Database use without SQL query evidence
boundaries: Does not imply database design, administration, or access-control policy

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: JavaScript can be used in frontend, backend, automation, and tooling; none of the current functional capabilities represents language-specific implementation.

new_capability.label: JavaScript development
new_capability.definition: Implementation and maintenance of software in the JavaScript programming language.
does_not_prove: Use of a JavaScript application without implementation
boundaries: Does not imply frontend, backend, or full-stack scope without context

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: TypeScript is a language used across frontend and backend contexts, while current capabilities are functional rather than language-specific.

new_capability.label: TypeScript development
new_capability.definition: Implementation and maintenance of typed JavaScript software using TypeScript.
does_not_prove: Use of a TypeScript application without implementation
boundaries: Does not imply frontend, backend, or full-stack scope without context

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Java requirements can concern backend, Android, desktop, or platform work; current capabilities cover only some contexts.

new_capability.label: Java development
new_capability.definition: Implementation and maintenance of software in the Java programming language.
does_not_prove: Use of a Java application without implementation
boundaries: Does not imply backend or Android scope without context

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: C# is explicitly distinct from the existing C/C++ capability and can be used across backend, desktop, game, and other contexts.

new_capability.label: C# development
new_capability.definition: Implementation and maintenance of software in the C# programming language.
boundaries: Does not imply backend, desktop, or game-development scope without context

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: A MongoDB requirement may cover document modeling, querying, integration, or operations. Database design alone is too narrow and generic data processing is not equivalent.

new_capability.label: MongoDB engineering
new_capability.definition: Application development, data modeling, querying, or operational engineering using MongoDB.
does_not_prove: Use of a MongoDB-backed application without MongoDB work
boundaries: Does not automatically imply relational schema design or generic data engineering

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Node.js can support APIs, command-line tools, build systems, and services; backend API development is not unconditional.

new_capability.label: Node.js development
new_capability.definition: Implementation and maintenance of JavaScript or TypeScript software running on Node.js.
does_not_prove: Use of Node-based tooling without Node.js implementation
boundaries: Does not imply API or full-stack delivery without context

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Ansible automation spans configuration management and infrastructure automation; product configuration and CI/CD do not cover that boundary.

new_capability.label: Infrastructure and configuration automation
new_capability.definition: Automating infrastructure provisioning or system configuration through declarative code, playbooks, or equivalent controlled automation.
does_not_prove: CI/CD pipeline use without infrastructure automation
boundaries: Separates infrastructure/configuration automation from application delivery pipelines

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Endpoint management and patch/compliance operations are not represented by generic product configuration, daily operations, or exploit handling.

new_capability.label: Enterprise endpoint management
new_capability.definition: Managing enterprise endpoint inventory, configuration, patching, compliance, and software deployment through endpoint-management platforms.
does_not_prove: Application configuration without endpoint fleet responsibility
boundaries: Does not imply vulnerability research or generic cloud administration

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Distributed-systems architecture covers coordination, partitioning, consistency, resilience, and scale beyond messaging, APIs, or data-oriented programming.

new_capability.label: Distributed systems engineering
new_capability.definition: Designing or implementing systems whose components coordinate across process or network boundaries with explicit consistency, resilience, and scaling concerns.
does_not_prove: Use of a message broker without distributed-system design responsibility
boundaries: Requires explicit distributed coordination, consistency, resilience, or scale context

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Network admission and access policy is distinct from database authorization, packet analysis, and DNS/DHCP fundamentals.

new_capability.label: Network access control
new_capability.definition: Designing, administering, or enforcing network admission, segmentation, authentication, and device-access policy.
boundaries: Excludes application and database authorization unless network admission is explicit

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Business-intelligence modeling and visualization are not equivalent to data cleaning or transformation.

new_capability.label: Business intelligence and analytics
new_capability.definition: Building governed analytical models, reports, dashboards, and decision-support views using business-intelligence tooling.
does_not_prove: Data cleaning without reporting or analysis
boundaries: Separates analytical delivery from upstream data processing

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Business-intelligence visualization is not represented by the current data-processing capability.

profiles.contextual_guidance: Decompose service plus activity when present; otherwise retain recognized-unmapped/manual status.

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Azure spans application, infrastructure, data, identity, and operations services. A platform mention cannot support one universal capability relationship.
profiles.contextual_guidance: Decompose service plus activity when present; otherwise retain recognized-unmapped/manual status.

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: GCP spans application, infrastructure, data, ML, and operations services. A platform mention cannot support one universal capability relationship.
profiles.contextual_guidance: Decompose service plus activity when present; otherwise retain recognized-unmapped/manual status.

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: .NET is a broad platform spanning backend, desktop, mobile, cloud, and game workloads. It cannot map universally to one current capability.
profiles.contextual_guidance: Use C#, ASP.NET, MAUI, Unity, or another contextual technology/activity when available.

profiles.why_existing_insufficient: Elasticsearch may be used for search, observability, analytics, or data storage. None is an unconditional relationship.
profiles.contextual_guidance: Require search, logging/observability, analytics, or storage context before capability resolution.
